text:
PACKET-02: UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context before or during this reading revealed a proposed identification, a catalogue entry, an edition or an earlier transcription for this packet. I read only the reader brief, PROMPT.md and the 35 image files in packet-02. I did not open packet.json and used no web or search tool. I did not try to identify the work or author. Proper names in the text (yo9 [name abbreviation], ysidorus, ypocras, boecius?, tullius?, hesiodus?, plato) are transcribed as written and are not identifications.
Beyond the rules: I listed the packet directory once to learn the file names. I kept a temporary working draft beside this file while reading and deleted it after assembling this response.

GENERAL OBSERVATIONS (all faces)
- 35 images = 9 faces. Each face has one reduced overview (image-001, -005, -009, -013, -017, -021, -025, -029, -033) followed by 2-3 overlapping native tiles (top/middle/bottom). Face I has two tiles.
- Every face is written in a single column, ca. 30-41 lines, in one small cursive bookhand in brown ink, with heavy abbreviation: "q(ue)" with a sinuous stroke, "(con)" written as a 9-like sign, "(er)go" as g with a stroke, superscript vowels.
- There are no rubrics, no coloured initials and no running titles anywhere. New sections are marked by three indented lines with an empty space for an initial and a small guide letter in the margin (B: "h"; C: "q"; D: unclear), or on face H by a plain enlarged capital "I". The line before a new section ends with ": ~".
- Numbered subdivisions use ordinals (2o, 3o, 4o ...) after "/" or "//". The ordinal digits are often ambiguous (the h-shaped form could be 4 or 5).
- A modern stamp "BIBLIOTHECA GANDAVENSIS" is in the lower margin of each face (or shows through reversed).
- Face I ends a text with a faint "Explicit" and blank space below.
- Tentative, from content only: a moral treatise built on numbered comparisons and exempla. Topics are fasting and moderation in food (faces G, A, B), human life compared to a river, smoke and a tree (B, C), restoring life by cultivating a vine (C, D), and the confessor compared to a physician (D/E, F, I). Face H covers twofold fasting, spiritual and bodily. It cross-refers to other treatises ("in tractatu de penitentia", "de gula", "de auaritia"). The faces are given here in packet order. Possible original sequence, by content only: G -> A -> B -> C -> D -> E -> F -> ... I. Face H (a new chapter on fasting) may belong before G. This is unverified.

CONVENTIONS: (abc) = proposed expansion; word(?) = uncertain reading; [illegible] = unread; [cut] = line runs past the image/leaf edge; [.] = lost letters at a damaged edge. Line numbers count from the top of the tile named. Lines repeated across overlapping tiles are given only once.

FACE A (overview image-001; tiles image-002 top, image-003 middle, image-004 bottom)

Layout survey (observation): single column, ca. 39 lines, no running title visible, no rubrics or enlarged initials on this face. Text is a small, informal cursive bookhand in brown ink, heavily abbreviated. Paragraph/section breaks marked inline by slash-like strokes ("/") and capitalised words. Library stamp "BIBLIOTHECA GANDAVENSIS" in lower margin (modern). Left edge damaged (loss near lines 8-9 on image-002 has not affected text). Right edge: final letters of many lines are cut by the image edge or the leaf edge. No marginal glosses seen. Tentative: continuous prose treatise with exempla (narrated stories) and authority citations.

Tiles overlap: image-003 repeats image-002 lines 12-15; image-004 repeats image-003 lines 21-24. Line numbers below are counted within the tile cited; repeats are not counted twice.
